title: #15: one issuer per ticket - the issuer holds a per-ticket lock for its life and the controller honours it
objective: While an issuer of ticket N is alive, a second issuer of N refuses to run and the controller neither releases N nor dispatches it again.
outline: A new module core/ticketlock.py (the flock pattern is slots._try): path(cfg, ident) = os.path.join(cfg.worktree_root, 'locks', 'issuer-%s.lock' % ident); take(cfg, ident) -> a held handle or None (os.open O_RDWR|O_CREAT, flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, never unlink); held(cfg, ident) -> True when LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on a fresh open of the path raises BlockingIOError (on success unlock and close at once). ticket_issuer.main(): right after Config() and before Issuer(...) and the try/finally that drops the live record, take the lock; None -> print one line ('ticket_issuer: #N already has a live issuer: lock <path> is held; nothing done') and return 2. Keep the handle referenced until main returns (Python fds are close-on-exec, agents do not inherit it). ticket_controller.finish_jobs: before _release_orphan, a held lock means the issuer lives: drop an exited child from self.children and leave the ticket. ticket_controller.dispatch: skip a ready ticket whose lock is held; it is dispatched on a later tick (the tick still counts as busy, like a running ticket, because the holder is a live process that ends). held() takes the lock for a moment; the controller probes only tickets it is not starting at that moment, so it never makes its own new issuer refuse. Docs: in devloop/README.md, the paragraph that starts 'A controller stopped with SIGTERM or SIGINT leaves its issuers' gets the lock, the exit-2 refusal and 'a held lock counts as a live issuer whatever the stamp says'; the exit line of ticket_issuer.py's docstring names the refusal.

notes: Measured on 2026-11-24 with the loop harness (opener scratch tests, kept at /home/user/agent-control-devloop/runs/creator/2026-11-24T133548Z-a1/repro/; copy them under tests_devloop/ of a scratch worktree and run them with run_tests.py to see the old behaviour): (a) SIGTERM to `ticket_controller.py --forever` alone: the issuer lives on and the next controller adopts it; no second issuer. (b) SIGTERM to the issuer while its agent wrapper ignores SIGTERM: kill_tree SIGKILLs the agent's process group after its 5 s grace, the issuer releases the ticket (ready, round - 1) and exits after 6.2 s; an interrupted issuer does not go on working. (c) A restarted controller that judges a live issuer's stamp dead (fixture: the stamp's boot rewritten while the issuer ran) releases the ticket ('issuer ended without an outcome; dispatch again') and starts a second issuer (round 2) in the same worktree while the first goes on (it next started round 3: T's 'old r3, new r2'); the second merged, landed and removed t1 and t1-cases; the first's next agent start failed 'no command for worker could start (cannot start sh: not found ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: <wt>/t1))' (T's #14 text) and it wrote stuck over the landed ticket. (p1) A second `ticket_issuer.py --id 1 --target int/g1` started by hand while the first ran claimed the ticket, merged within 3 s (rc 0); the first then wrote feedback, round start and stuck over the merged ticket (rc 1). (p2) A ticket set to ready under a running issuer (what _release_orphan writes) was merged by that issuer anyway: int/g1 moved, ready became merged, rc 0. Not measured: which part of T's macOS stamp the controller judged dead (boot id = the text of `sysctl -n kern.boottime`, or the host name); the lock makes it irrelevant, since the kernel frees a flock only when its holder dies. This ticket stops the second issuer at its source; the ownership ticket of the same hand-in makes an issuer that lost its ticket stop writing. Out of scope: an agent process that left its wrapper's process group (setsid) outlives the issuer's kill_tree (measured: the issuer still exits after 6.2 s). Never write os.kill, killpg, pkill or the text 'kill -' in any added line (code, tests, comments, strings): board/config.json hard_block matches them and stops the ticket before merge. Use osx.alive, osx.kill_tree, Popen.terminate or Popen.send_signal instead. Group new-g1: the four #14/#15 tickets share files and one regression.
acceptance: ticket_issuer.py holds an exclusive BSD flock (fcntl.flock LOCK_EX) on <devloop.worktrees>/locks/issuer-<N>.lock (folder created when missing; the file is never deleted or replaced) from before its claim until the process exits: while its worker runs, fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) on that path from another process raises BlockingIOError; after the issuer has exited it succeeds.

When another process holds that lock, `ticket_issuer.py --id N --target T` exits 2 within 10 s with exactly one non-empty stderr line that contains `#N` and the lock file's path, and changes nothing: the pool repository's HEAD is the same commit before and after, no worktree <devloop.worktrees>/t<N> is created, and a live record <devloop.worktrees>/runs/live/issuer-<N>.json that existed before still exists with the same bytes.

Controller.finish_jobs leaves a running ticket as it is (state running, `run` unchanged, no event 'issuer ended without an outcome; dispatch again') while its issuer lock is held by another process, also when osx.stamp_dead(ticket['run']) is True (for example a stamp whose boot is not osx.boot_id()).

Controller.dispatch does not call start_issuer for a ready ticket whose issuer lock is held by another process, although the ticket could start now in its open group; once the lock is free, the next dispatch calls start_issuer for it.
With the lock free, finish_jobs judges the stamp as today: a dead stamp releases the ticket, a live one is adopted (issuers started before this change hold no lock).

The user asked for these (2026-11-24: 「修新issue」). Each ticket names its issue number(s) in its title so the main session can close the issues after landing. Issue texts are quoted or summarised here; they are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file for a new area), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file. Each case should run in seconds. Grouping: place these as you judge (core/chain.py); #14 and #15 may share a cause, #16 is about groups.

## Issue #15: a restarted controller starts a second issuer for a running ticket
T (A at b5564f9, macOS): after a controller restart done as #11's answer recommends (SIGTERM to `ticket_controller.py --forever` only, children left running), the old issuer of #320 (pid 84547, started by the previous controller, ppid 1 after the restart, running r3-worker through a wrapper `alternate.sh -> agy.sh`) was not adopted: the new controller started a second `ticket_issuer.py --id 320` (pid 66766), which ran an r2-worker in the same worktree `t320` on `t/320`. The r2 worker saw the other run and handed in `blocked`; #320 went stuck. The orphan then began merging main into t/320 (20:15:17 local). It ignored SIGTERM (agy.sh waits for agy) and had to be SIGKILLed.
What the main session read in the code (inference, not measured):
- The controller adopts a live issuer by the ticket's `run` stamp (ticket_controller.py finish_jobs, osx.stamp_dead). A second issuer can only start after the ticket is back to ready: `_release_orphan` (stamp judged dead) or the issuer's own `release()` on a signal (ticket_issuer.py _go, Interrupted), which sets ready and round-1. The new issuer running r2 while the old one ran r3 fits the second: the old issuer got a signal, released the ticket (r3 -> round 2), and then did not exit - its interrupted_costs/stop_agents path may block on a wrapper that ignores SIGTERM, or the process went on to the merge step.
- Find out which, by reproducing with the loop harness (a fake agent command that ignores SIGTERM; stop the controller as T did; also signal the issuer). Write the measured cause in the ticket.
Wanted:
- A ticket never has two issuers at once: the issuer holds a per-ticket lock (flock on a file under the worktrees root, like gitx's worktree lock) for its whole life; a second issuer for the same id refuses at once (exit 2, one line) and touches nothing.
- An issuer that has released its ticket (interrupted) does no further work on it: no merge, no push, no pool write other than the release; it stops its agents' process trees (kill_tree, escalating to SIGKILL after a short grace when a wrapper ignores SIGTERM) and exits.
- A restarted controller adopts a live issuer (stamp alive) and does not dispatch the ticket again while that issuer (or its lock) lives.

## Issue #14: a ticket's worktree disappears during a chain fall-through after quota
T: three cases on 2026-11-24 (#369 reviewer, #351 worker, #354 reviewer): the first command of the role's chain (agy.sh) said "usage limit reached"; about 3 minutes later the next command (claude) could not start: `no command for reviewer could start (cannot start claude: not found ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../tabby_pool_wt/devloop/t369'))`. By then `t369` and `t369-cases` were gone and not in `git worktree list`. The ticket went stuck.
Inference (main session, not measured): the cases were the same afternoon as #15; a second issuer for the same ticket that ends (stuck) runs `Issuer.cleanup()` and removes the worktrees the first issuer still uses. Check this first; if it is not the cause, find what removed the worktree (grep every remove_worktree / prune / rmtree caller).
Wanted:
- A ticket's worktree survives a quota wait and a chain fall-through (nothing but its own issuer removes it, and only at its end).
